disposition: No blocker found in the narrow exact-record access acknowledgment repair.

invariants.name: Only the same invocation can acknowledge its consumed challenge
invariants.evidence: expectedConsumption is a private closure set only after current purpose/pending/expiry checks. Recovery requires that invocation’s fresh random sessionHash and every consumed-row scalar field to match exactly. A later POST starts with expectedConsumption=null and a different sessionHash; a foreign/concurrent consumed row cannot pass.

invariants.name: Challenge and session create acknowledgments require exact fresh records
invariants.evidence: The challenge and session keys are fresh256-bit random values. sameAccessRecord requires the same own-key count and exact scalar values for email, purpose/scope, status, creation, expiry and optional intake binding. Changed/revoked/conflicting records throw rather than being overwritten or reactivated.

invariants.name: Purpose, expiry and revocation remain enforced
invariants.evidence: Wrong-purpose or initially expired challenges still fail before consumption. A same-invocation acknowledgment recognizes a consumption already accepted before expiry; it does not rewrite or extend challenge expiry. Session creation/expiry is fixed once before the write retry, and revoked/different session rows cannot match active expectedSession. getAccessSession still requires active status, current expiry and exact scope.

invariants.name: No existing bearer is disclosed and replay remains rejected
invariants.evidence: The only returned bearer is the newly generated local session value after its exact expected session record is confirmed. The patch does not read or return another stored raw bearer. Later/concurrent requests cannot reuse the private expected-consumption state; the recorded concurrent result is one200/one410.

scope: Only access.mjs runtime behavior changes. Generic atomicUpdate, memory-storage policy, provider execution gates, webhook/routing and public error disclosure are unchanged.
